summary: @ai-support-agent/cli exposes installer host to remote shell/PTY and command execution over vendor WebSocket
details: When the CLI is started with `ai-support-agent start`, it opens an authenticated WebSocket to `wss://api.ai-support-agent.com/ws/agent-terminal` and pipes incoming `stdin` messages (base64-decoded) directly into a node-pty-spawned shell running in the project directory (dist/vscode/vscode-server.js and related runtime code). The same runtime polls `/api/<tenant>/agent/commands/pending` and dispatches server-issued handlers including `server_setup_exec` (Ansible playbook execution), `ssh_exec`, `sync_repository`, `reboot`, and `update`. The combined effect is a persistent remote-administration channel: whoever controls (or compromises) the vendor API endpoint or the bearer token can execute arbitrary shell commands, SSH into other hosts using stored credentials, and reboot or reconfigure the installer's machine. The remote control surface is the package's core runtime behavior rather than a hidden payload, but it constitutes full-host RCE by design and is only as trustworthy as the vendor's server integrity and token custody.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
